clue.text: Good Friday: Banquo's army routed by lord of tavern

indicators.note: an army that is routed is scattered in disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
the calendar abbreviation for Friday
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Holy Week battle scene in which Banquo's soldiers are put to flight, as if Macbeth had spilled into the Easter story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marquis of Granby, an eighteenth-century general, gave his name to hundreds of English pubs, so he is literally a lord of the tavern sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis of Granby is one of the most common pub names in England, so the nobleman presides over many inns.

clue.text: Shrill in complaining of southern weapon

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: Someone moaning loudly about a weapon from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident describes a harsh, loud, grating voice, the kind used when protesting or making demands.

clue.text: Environmentally friendly chap, a runner

blocks.note: green describes ecological concern
as in the old British form of address 'old bean'

explanation.surface: An eco-conscious man who goes running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A runner' looks like the jogger the chap is; it is the runner bean, a climbing vegetable common in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Runner beans are eaten as pods while unripe, making them one variety of the green bean family of vegetables.

clue.text: Supported by press, actors are impregnable

blocks.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Actors who enjoy good reviews from the newspapers are beyond attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supported by' puts the actors on top of the press, so the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron case or alibi is one so solid it cannot be broken or challenged.

clue.text: Witch doctor, not the genuine article

blocks.note: a sham is a fake, something not genuine
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sneer that a tribal healer is a fraud, not the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The genuine article' reads as one idiom, but it splits: 'not the genuine' is one piece and 'article' is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spiritual intermediary, commonly called a witch doctor in older English.

clue.text: They won't see the way to separate love from wealth

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
ST is the abbreviation for street
riches are wealth

explanation.surface: A moral about what keeps love apart from money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To separate ... from' places the way between love and wealth. Ostriches are proverbially said to bury their heads in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich supposedly hides its head in sand to avoid danger, so it stands for anyone refusing to face facts.

clue.text: Creator of pilgrim sounding footsore?

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is spoken like the one meaning footsore, not spelt like it

blocks.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: The author of a journey on foot whose name suggests aching feet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress, whose hero Christian walks a long road.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress, so he invented its pilgrim hero, Christian.

clue.text: 15 represent them in the case of landlord at shindig

blocks.note: re means concerning, in the case of
a publican is the landlord of a pub
a shindig is a lively party

explanation.surface: Elephants standing for a pub landlord's court case, an absurd scene after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is ELEPHANTS; the elephant is the emblem of the US Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant has been the symbol of the American Republican Party since Thomas Nast's cartoons in the 1870s.

clue.text: A mathematician keeping time with hospital as sequel

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the mathematician's name wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Pierre de Fermat, of the Last Theorem
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A mathematician staying in hospital, as a follow-up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden math in 'mathematician' is a decoy: the mathematician is Fermat, who holds the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the consequence or period following an event, so it comes as a sequel to it.

clue.text: Every man for himself: queue up at sixes ... and sevens

indicators.note: at sixes and sevens means in total confusion, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
six is VI in Roman numerals, so sixes is VIs

explanation.surface: A disorderly queue where everyone looks after themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis splits the idiom 'at sixes and sevens': 'at' and 'sixes' supply letters, and only 'and sevens' is left to signal the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauve qui peut is French for 'save who can', a cry for a disorderly flight in which each looks after himself.

clue.text: See 10
NB: spoil the queue for an audience

indicators.note: something done for an audience is heard rather than read, so we go by what the word sounds like

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
the word queue said aloud is the letter K followed by you

explanation.surface: A note warning someone not to disrupt the line waiting for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: NB stands for nota bene, 'note well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark you is an old-fashioned spoken equivalent of nota bene, calling attention to what follows.

clue.text: Going steady? Let 'em 'ave it!

blocks.note: first meaning: a couple in a relationship
second meaning: a dropped-aitch command to hit them

explanation.surface: Someone gives the go-ahead to a pair who are dating.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so 'let 'em 'ave it' (attack them) becomes 'it 'em, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people described as an item are in a recognised romantic relationship, the slang for going steady.

clue.text: Thousand pound container for a pound in Venice

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a can holds things
taken as written
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Buying an expensive box at a bargain price on a Venetian holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canal is the main waterway running through the centre of the Italian city.

clue.text: Peel off county and church and I would find Kipling's little giant

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters need to be put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county
CH is the abbreviation for church
I'ld is the old Shakespearean contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pilgrimage through a shire and its church to discover a character from Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel off' reads as strip away; 'off' is the anagram signal. The modern I'd would leave the grid a letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elephant's Child is the curious young elephant in Kipling's Just So Stories, small for an elephant yet still huge.

clue.text: Bunting from Windsor to Lancaster

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the three words

explanation.surface: Flags hung along a road from one royal town to another, as for a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunting looks like festive flags, but it is the bird; Windsor and Lancaster are both royal houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family, notorious as a French delicacy.

clue.text: Mournful blend of gale and ice

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bleak winter weather of wind and frost that feels sorrowful.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means in the manner of an elegy, a poem of lament, so it describes sorrowful expression.

clue.text: Means of hatching, for example, to put into barbarian

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the small word goes within the barbarian

blocks.note: the abbreviation of exempli gratia
the Goths were the barbarians who sacked Rome
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan for hatching a scheme by recruiting a barbarian.
explanation.walkthrough: TO goes after the first letter of the barbarian, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg tooth is a small hard tip on the beak or snout of a hatchling, used to break through the shell.

clue.text: 8, for example, has one that is goodly when revised

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a political party's platform looks pleasant once it has been edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is REPUBLICAN PARTY: a political party, for example, has an ideology.
explanation.definitionFit: Every political party holds a body of doctrines and beliefs that guide its policies, which is its ideology.

clue.text: Ram in cherry tree maddened dog with energy

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the ram sits within the tree
something maddened is driven wild, so its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the gean is the wild cherry
a tup is a ram
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of a ram caught in a cherry tree while a frantic dog races about.
explanation.walkthrough: Gean and tup are country words: the wild cherry and a breeding ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is informal for vigour and enthusiasm, the drive that makes someone active.

clue.text: One of two, for example, turning up with a bit of conscience?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a twin is one of a pair born together
the abbreviation of exempli gratia

explanation.surface: One twin appearing with a guilty feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge of conscience is a brief pang of guilt, a small sharp feeling of remorse.

clue.text: You will be surprised to hear as much?

definitions.text: You will be surprised to hear

blocks.clueFragment: You will be surprised to hear
blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation stressing something remarkable, as in 'the Queen
second meaning: the same amount, not a smaller one

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single question about how surprising some news is; the phrase both expresses that surprise and means an equal quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is added to highlight a surprising detail, and literally means an amount that is not smaller.

clue.text: See 3
See 15
A large 'allo for King David's girl

blocks.note: taken as written
big means large
a greeting with its aitch dropped, so hail loses its H

explanation.surface: A big hello in Cockney for the king's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''allo' signals the dropped H: the matching greeting is hail, which becomes 'ail.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail was the widow of Nabal who became one of King David's wives in the First Book of Samuel.

clue.text: Work hard on lamb that was drowned?

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Toiling over a lamb that ended up in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not the animal but the writer Charles Lamb, who signed his essays Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia in Hamlet drowns in a brook after falling from a willow, so she is the one who drowned.

clue.text: Was father to request a time?

blocks.note: to beg is to request
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A father asking someone for the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Begat is the archaic past tense of beget, the verb used in Biblical genealogies for fathering children.

clue.text: Group to get off when torched?

blocks.note: a set is a group
to alight is to get off a bus or train

explanation.surface: Passengers made to leave a vehicle that has been set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something alight is to set fire to it, which is what torching a building means.
